Posterior parameter summaries

summary.magComp.Rd

Summarizes posterior draws. summary(fit, ...) calls samples(fit, ...) and then summarizes that sample object. The default reports scalar parameters; use type = "effects" or type = "combined" for individual effects or combined coefficients. Multiple-chain fits include the classical unsplit Gelman-Rubin \(\widehat{R}\) diagnostic; single-chain fits report NA for \(\widehat{R}\). Effective sample size is computed from within-chain autocorrelation and summed across chains, without a between-chain correction. The R-hat calculation is bounded below by one and does not split or rank-normalize chains. See the technical guide's Diagnostics section in magComp-package for the formulas.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'magComp'
summary(object, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), ...)

# S3 method for class 'magCompSamples'
summary(object, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted magComp object or an object returned by samples().

probs

Nonempty numeric vector of posterior quantile probabilities strictly between zero and one.

...

For a fitted model, arguments passed to samples(), including type, start, thin, chains, combine_chains, and group. Unused for an already extracted sample object.

Value

A data frame of class magCompSummary, identifying component, block, term, parameter, index, and manuscript symbol, followed by posterior means, standard deviations, requested quantiles, \(\widehat{R}\), effective sample size, retained samples per chain, and number of chains.

Details

Parameter names match the public sample entries: coefficients, size, variance, loadings, and covariance parameter names such as phi, lambda, and nu. The index column identifies the relevant design column, stick/covariate pair, stick/factor pair, or factor. Component, block, and term identities stay the same as in magCompSettings and samples. Symbols use portable ASCII notation. Fixed size and covariance values are excluded; positive anchor-diagonal loadings are included as estimated parameters. Fixed upper-anchor zeros are omitted from the scalar summary. Latent effects and scores are available through summary(fit, type = "effects"). Combined coefficients also identify their fitted unit or group, coefficient, allocation row, and parent context. R-hat and ESS use the selected draws within their original chains, even when storage has been pooled. One-chain selections report NA for R-hat.
